newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends unchanged, c. bank sells dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends unchanged, c. bank sells dlrs.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed unchanged at 28 to the dollar on Friday as the central bank stepped in to sell dollars an hour before the close, traders said.
Traders said the central bank sold only about $3-5 million at 28 pesos to influence trading after the peso lost ground from its day-high of 27.80.
The peso generally showed more strength during the day, with the average rate at 28.142 from the the previous 28.574. Volume was lower at $144.2 million from $194.5 million.
"This was a carryover from yesterday," a foreign bank dealer said. "Dollars in the system have started to unload after the peso gained strength in recent days."
This is the fifth day of trading since the central bank allowed the peso to move in a wider band in an effective devaluation.
"We will see a trading range of 27.5/28.50 next week," a trader said.
Traders said they expect more dollar selling by investors as the initial fears from the central bank's new policy subside.
The central bank had slashed its overnight borrowing rate twice in the past two days to 25 percent as the peso had begun to normalise.
